If a support relation is transitive, supported blocks are closed under multiplication. Conversely, to detect a missing compositional edge from universal multiplication closure, one needs blocks whose composite is nonzero. Contract row 25 works over a field, with every packet range nontrivial and arbitrary packet-Hom blocks available. Those hypotheses provide the witnesses used by the converse.

A zero packet can make a relation edge mathematically invisible. The mathematical text therefore explicitly includes the necessary nonzero-packet assumptions in its $*$-support and source-component-count corollaries. Row 25 has its own nontriviality scope. The twenty-file foundational formalization retains that scope.

The reachability module first shows that word orbits of packet-supported seeds remain in the support reachable from those seeds. Seed rank depends on an acting algebra. It is not simply vector space dimension. One vector generates the natural module of a full matrix algebra, whereas a scalar action on $k^n$ needs $n$ independent generators.
The foundational definitions use the existing span-rank API for the top submodule.

The cardinal-valued rank makes sense without finite generation. The natural-valued \code{seedFinrank} is the finite-generation minimum only under the hypotheses used by the finite-rank theorems. The zero module has rank zero. The cyclic/rank-one equivalence therefore includes a nontriviality hypothesis.
\subsection{The one-seed presentation}
The first isomorphism theorem then supplies the quotient-to-range equivalence.

For a noncommutative acting algebra, the kernel here is a left submodule of the regular module. The theorem does not promote it to a two-sided ideal. Likewise, no norm or bounded completion is manufactured by this algebraic construction. The analytic completion result needs a supplied continuous isometry with dense range.

For several seeds, \code{Finsupp.linearCombination} evaluates a finitely supported coefficient family. This works for arbitrary label types. The finite-minimum theorem states that, when the module is finitely generated, its seed finrank is the least $n$ admitting a surjection from \code{Fin n →₀ A}.

Under a surjective semilinear map $f:M\to N$ along $\sigma:A\to B$, an $A$-generating set maps to a $B$-generating set. Coefficients in the image of $\sigma$ are already available in $B$, so the rank inequality does not require $\sigma$ itself to be onto. An equality statement requires more: either the scalar map is surjective or the target action is literally restricted to the image algebra.

The tensor theorem proves an upper bound under its stated commuting-action and scalar-tower laws. The scalar-quotient theorem gives a lower bound when the action on a finite-dimensional quotient factors through a character. A dimension bound for an arbitrary quotient would be a different statement.
\subsection{The split-semisimple formula}

For a finite product of blocks, independent actions combine by the maximum. \code{SemisimpleCompletion} connects these row-space arguments to \code{seedRank}. The abstract theorem consumes an algebra equivalence to the product of full matrix algebras and a compatible semilinear module equivalence to the product of matrix modules.

The output is a rank formula for the supplied realization. This preserved 20-file component does not derive a Wedderburn decomposition from an arbitrary semisimple algebra, nor the nonsplit division-algebra form. The later continuation supplies that existence integration and the nonsplit formula, as described in Section~\ref{sec:release-current}. A reader applying historical row 10 should still identify its supplied equivalences before quoting its conclusion.
\subsection{Single-operator seed number: the upper and lower halves}

The proof constructs an \code{IsLeast} pair. Its first component is the padded generating family. Its second component takes an arbitrary generating family and uses the quotient at \code{maxEigen} to force its cardinality to be at least $R$. The existence of these quotient and extraction certificates is an input. The file does not independently construct general Jordan form or Chinese-remainder primary projectors from a bare matrix.

Row 14 derives the four-way cyclicity statement after two canonical-form bridges have been supplied: geometric multiplicity agrees with block multiplicity, and equality of minimal and characteristic polynomials is equivalent to one block per eigenvalue. Lean verifies their use in the equivalence chain. It does not reconstruct those bridges from arbitrary matrix data in this component.

The row is marked stronger because its compiled implication omits a separately inherited finite-label hypothesis from the manuscript. Stronger refers to this precise change in the typed statement. It does not mean that the supplied canonical-form hypotheses disappeared.

For the path, the endpoint Krylov matrix has zero entries below its diagonal and ones on the diagonal: a walk of length $r$ cannot reach a vertex farther than $r$, and exactly one length-$r$ walk reaches vertex $r$. Hence its determinant is one. This yields cyclicity without a numerical eigendecomposition.

For cycles, two adjacent delta vectors generate by the adjacency recurrence. Over $\mathbb C$, two distinct Fourier characters with the same adjacency eigenvalue provide a two-dimensional scalar quotient, supplying the lower bound. The resulting minimum-two theorem applies to the simple cycle on $n+3$ vertices.
\subsection{Bounded packets and closed-hull obstructions}

A continuous surjection intertwining the stated operator families sends a dense source hull to a dense target hull. Dense range already suffices for that density conclusion. Exact equality of a source packet's image with a target packet requires the surjectivity used by the packet-range theorem. Neither conclusion needs an unspoken open-mapping argument.

The bilateral shift result uses an actual reindexing representation on $\ell^2(\mathbb Z)$, not an assumed abstract shift action. Its translates of $\delta_0$ recover all delta vectors, whose linear span is dense. The final statement says that one is the least finite seed cardinality for dense generation by this representation. It does not establish an unrestricted cardinal-valued Laurent-algebra rank.

The proof's termination argument uses the Noetherian property of the submodule lattice. It establishes existence of a stopping index and correctness of the stopped subspace. It does not extract a basis-maintenance loop, a decidable rank test, or a complexity bound. Those belong to an implementation refinement that would require its own proof.

The transfer-block specification is similarly exact at the mathematical level: its table consists of the blocks, summing it gives the original map, and its support predicate is block nonvanishing. It does not verify floating-point tolerances or a sparse edge-list generator.

The exact graph-rank specification takes the finite-spectrum maximum of exact eigenspace dimensions. Its correctness theorem consumes an eigenbasis, projector-polynomial data, spectrum coverage, eigenspace dimensions, and an attained maximum. Its definition is marked \code{noncomputable}. A Python experiment and this specification can support the same formula while remaining different forms of evidence.

It constructs quotient and quadratic normal-form realizations, explicit two-coefficient packet coordinates, and multiplication operators. It proves the relation $M_y^2=M_x^3-M_x$ and one-seed generation of the regular module.

The coefficient projectors are linear over the ground field, but not over the full coordinate algebra. The file contains explicit witnesses to that failure. This is an instructive type boundary: the acting algebra for generation may be larger than the scalar algebra over which packet maps are linear. The zero-entry check matters: an audit that accidentally imports nothing must fail. The final count is a count of entries in the environment, not a count of handwritten mathematical theorems. The separate mapped-target pass resolves each of the eighty-four names, prints its type, and checks its axiom report.

The allowlisted principles are standard Lean/Mathlib foundations. The audit does not claim axiom-free mathematics in an absolute sense. It also does not prove historical priority, performance claims, or the absence of defects in the compiler, trusted kernel, or dependency cache. These are the ordinary boundaries of the recorded verification method, not gaps secretly filled by the count of mapped declarations.

candidate_lines.text: \Needspace{10\baselineskip}\subsection{Row 1: Universal one-seed presentation}

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} For the module map \code{a ↦ a • s}, the quotient by its kernel is linearly equivalent to its exact range; the glue theorem verifies that the class of \code{a} maps to \code{a • s}; and singleton generation is equivalent to surjectivity. If the induced map from the normed quotient is supplied as a continuous linear isometry with dense range into a Banach target, it extends uniquely to a continuous linear equivalence from the completion and intertwines supplied bounded operators.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Boundary.} No norm, isometry, density, or bounded extension is constructed automatically on the algebraic quotient. The annihilator is only the typed left submodule/left-ideal object; no two-sided ideal claim is made.
\Needspace{10\baselineskip}\subsection{Row 2: Multi-seed presentation}

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} An arbitrary Finsupp-indexed family has the free-module quotient presentation; the glue theorem verifies that a coefficient family maps to its finite linear combination; and a generating family gives the quotient onto the whole module. For a finite module, \code{seedFinrank} is the least \code{n} admitting a surjection from \code{Fin n →₀ A}.
\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Boundary.} The natural-valued minimum is asserted only under module finiteness. No finite basis or executable presentation matrix is produced.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} For every nontrivial module over a semiring, unrestricted cardinal-valued seed rank equals one exactly when a cyclic vector exists.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} For an arbitrary ring homomorphism \code{σ : A →+* B}, a surjective \code{σ}-semilinear map gives \code{seedRank B N ≤ seedRank A M}; \code{σ} need not be onto.
\Needspace{10\baselineskip}\subsection{Row 5: Image-algebra invariance}

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} For a \code{k}-algebra homomorphism \code{φ : A →ₐ[k] B} and a bijective \code{φ}-semilinear map, the target action is restricted literally to \code{φ.range}, and its seed rank equals the source seed rank.
\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Boundary.} Equality for the full target algebra \code{B} requires \code{φ} to be surjective; it is not inferred otherwise.
\Needspace{10\baselineskip}\subsection{Row 6: Shared direct-sum bound}
\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Boundary.} This is only an upper bound; it does not identify when equality holds.
\Needspace{10\baselineskip}\subsection{Row 7: Independent direct-sum formula}
\Needspace{10\baselineskip}\subsection{Row 8: Tensor-product bound}

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} Over a commutative semiring \code{k}, with the stated algebra/module, scalar-tower, and commuting-action laws, the action of \code{A ⊗[k] B} on \code{X ⊗[k] Y} satisfies the cardinal product bound and realizes \code{(a ⊗ b)(x ⊗ y) = ax ⊗ by}.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} For a field \code{k}, a character \code{χ : A →ₐ[k] k}, a finite-dimensional scalar module \code{Y}, and a surjective \code{χ}-semilinear map \code{X → Y}, \code{finrank k Y} is a cardinal lower bound for \code{seedRank A X}.
\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Boundary.} The target action must factor through the stated character; a general quotient does not yield the dimension bound.
\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Boundary.} Lean does not prove the existence of the Wedderburn/module decompositions, nor the nonsplit division-algebra variant.
\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} Over a field and for \code{n > 0}, every nonzero vector in the natural \code{M_n(k)}-module generates and the canonical cardinal seed rank is one.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} For \code{d > 0}, the left action of \code{M_d(k)} on the \code{d × m} matrix realization of \code{m} copies has seed rank \code{⌈m/d⌉}; every generating \code{r}-family satisfies \code{⌈m/d⌉ ≤ r}.
\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Boundary.} No general simple-module formula over a nontrivial endomorphism division algebra is included.
\Needspace{10\baselineskip}\subsection{Row 13: Single-operator seed rank}

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} Certificate-explicit: a finite label family supplies block generators, an attained bound \code{R}, joint polynomial-orbit generation, polynomial extraction from padded seeds, and surjective scalar quotient maps with the evaluation intertwining law. Then \code{R} is the least polynomial seed number and both \code{seedFinrank} and cardinal \code{seedRank} over the genuine image algebra \code{k[T] = Algebra.adjoin k {T}} equal \code{R}.

\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Boundary.} Lean does not construct a primary/Jordan decomposition, Chinese-remainder projectors, or identify the supplied multiplicities with \code{dim ker(T - λI)} from bare hypotheses.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} Certificate-explicit and finite-dimensional: from an exact positive seed-number certificate, a supplied equality between geometric and block multiplicities, and the supplied minpoly/charpoly canonical-form bridge, Lean proves the four-way equivalence among cyclicity, all geometric multiplicities one, one block per eigenvalue, and \code{minpoly = charpoly}. The compiled implication does not require the manuscript's separately inherited finite-label hypothesis.
\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Boundary.} Neither canonical-form bridge is derived by Lean from an arbitrary matrix; the theorem verifies the equivalence after those bridges are supplied.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} A finite complete, idempotent, pairwise-annihilating linear projector family gives mutually inverse analysis and finite-sum synthesis maps between the module and the independently defined dependent product of projector ranges.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} For a finite bounded projector family on a Banach space over a nontrivially normed field, all packet ranges are closed and analysis/synthesis form a continuous linear equivalence with the canonical finite dependent-product norm.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} If \code{M} is a dense submodule of a normed space and \code{P_i} is any bounded idempotent, the closure of \code{P_i(M)} equals the full range \code{P_i(X)}. The packet-family theorem is the direct specialization. No invariance of \code{M}, surrounding finite packet family, or completeness of \code{X} is required by the manuscript or the compiled declaration.
\par\smallskip\noindent\textbf{Boundary.} Boundedness is required; no unbounded-projector or infinite conditional-sum claim is made.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} The sum of all transfer blocks reconstructs an arbitrary linear map between modules carrying possibly different finite projector families; the endomorphism formula is the manuscript instance.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Exact scope.} The block of a composite is the finite sum of composite blocks, even for three different source/intermediate/target modules and projector families; the single-space operator identity is the manuscript instance.
